heroText: Abuja is Nigeria's purpose-built capital, planned in the 1980s around the dramatic granite outcrop of Aso Rock. First-time visitors should photograph Aso Rock from the Presidential Villa area, compare the Abuja National Mosque and National Christian Centre standing near each other, and stroll through Millennium Park's landscaped grounds. Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport sits southeast of the city, and the striking Zuma Rock monolith makes an easy day trip north.

areas.name: Maitama
areas.text: Maitama is Abuja's most affluent district, home to upscale hotels, embassies and views toward Aso Rock.

areas.name: Asokoro
areas.text: Asokoro is the diplomatic quarter, home to foreign embassies and the Presidential Villa, close to Aso Rock.

areas.name: Wuse
areas.text: Wuse is Abuja's commercial hub, packed with shopping malls, restaurants and mid-range hotels.

areas.name: Garki
areas.text: Garki is the city's original central business district, home to government offices, banks and Area 1 shopping.

airports.name: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (ABV)
airports.search: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, Nigeria
airports.text: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport lies about 20 kilometres southeast of the city centre; pre-booked transfers are recommended, especially for late arrivals.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (ABV) and central Abuja before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Maitama and Asokoro suit visitors wanting upscale hotels close to embassies and Aso Rock, while Wuse and Garki offer more central, mid-range options near shopping and business districts. Most of Abuja's main sights sit within a short drive of each other.
hotelIntro: Maitama holds Abuja's most upscale hotels near embassies and Aso Rock, Asokoro suits diplomatic visits, and Wuse or Garki offer better value with easy access to malls, restaurants and government offices.
rentalCars: A rental car or hired driver helps for reaching Zuma Rock and other sights outside the city, though taxis and ride-hailing apps cover central Abuja well.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Maitama or Asokoro for upscale hotels near embassies and Aso Rock, or Wuse for more central, better-value options.

travelTips.title: See both faiths side by side
travelTips.text: Visit the Abuja National Mosque and National Christian Centre together, since the two landmarks stand within sight of each other.

travelTips.title: Day trip to Zuma Rock
travelTips.text: Budget half a day for Zuma Rock, the giant granite monolith visible on the drive north from the city.

travelTips.title: Traffic planning
travelTips.text: Allow extra time for journeys during rush hour, since Abuja's wide roads can still see heavy congestion at peak times.

nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Zuma Rock, a dramatic 725-metre granite monolith, rises beside the highway roughly an hour north of Abuja.

nearbyIdeas.name: Gurara Falls

nearbyIdeas.text: Gurara Falls, about two hours from Abuja, offers a scenic waterfall and picnic spot popular for weekend day trips.
